Style guide v1 draft for the new Dr. James website, 3 October 2026. Colours, type, buttons, glass cards, service arch cards, credentials, step tracker, doctor card and the mobile action bar, using real content from drjamesp.com. Hover, click and swipe to try them. Yellow chips mark facts to confirm with Dr. James.

Build notes for the coding agent · read before building
  • Locked Fonts: Figtree (all UI and text) and Instrument Serif italic (one accent word per heading, at most). Load with next/font, self-hosted, preload only Figtree. Devanagari is not needed. Arabic (Noto Naskh Arabic) is proposed for Muscat and waits for approval.
  • Draft Colours: teal and navy are sampled from the Dr. James logo. Frankincense sand and the logo's silver are decorative only (arch hairlines, seal rings, glows, badge sparkles) and never text. Copy the :root tokens exactly once approved.
  • Signature shapes: the Omani arch from the logo (portrait face of the hero cube, sand hairlines) and the medallion bezel with sand ticks (service badges, credential seals). Service icons sit free on a soft glow, never inside a card or window.
  • One gradient surface per viewport: primary buttons, the active tab, the Book button and the mobile bar. Everything else is white with tints.
  • Hero: the credential cube (v3 below), approved direction. Portrait face first.
  • Location and rules: the practice is at Badr Al Samaa Royal Hospital, Muscat, Oman. The master prompt's India rules stay as the minimum standard (no testimonials, ratings, "best", cure claims or patient counters). Emergency line is 9999 (Oman). The client confirmed on 3 October 2026 that no hospital or ministry approval is needed for this site; keep the content rules anyway.
  • Draft Logo: redrawn as SVG from the AI PNG (horizontal, stacked, white and mark), shown in the Logo section for approval. Use the SVG files only, never the old PNG.
  • Mobile: any section with more than three cards becomes a self-moving swipe carousel below 768px (every 4.5s, pause on touch or hover, pause button, still under reduced motion).

Hero v3 rules
  • Ground: full-width deep navy (--night), two faint arches behind the cube and the logo's ECG line in sand, drawn once on load. The only dark surface on the page.
  • Cube: 360px desktop, 248px mobile. Faces are designed panels, not raw photos: frosted navy glass, a sand hairline inset frame, light edges. Portrait face first, so his face is what loads and what search previews show.
  • Motion: a quarter turn every 4s with a 1.2s ease, an idle float of 6px, a sheen across each face as it arrives, a slow sand orbit ring on the floor. Pauses on hover, focus, drag and hidden tab. Drag or arrow keys turn it. Under reduced motion it stays on the portrait and the tabs switch faces without animation.
  • Tabs: four pills under the cube with a sliding indicator; they are the accessible way to read every face (each face's text is also in the HTML for search).
  • Left column: name signature, eyebrow, H1, sub, buttons, three fact figures and the doctor chip. No floating chips; the cube carries the detail.
  • Buttons: Book (two-part) + "Call +968 9751 0975" + WhatsApp on desktop. On mobile: Book now + call icon + WhatsApp icon in ONE row.
  • Mobile order (390 x 844, all above the fold): eyebrow, H1 (34px), cube (210px) with tabs, the Book row, one short line. Name line, doctor chip and long sub are hidden on mobile; facts follow below the fold.
  • Doctor chip: "Physician-led care" with his avatar under the facts, desktop only.

Do

  • White page background everywhere; tints only for chips, tabs, washes and glows
  • One gradient surface per viewport
  • Teal text #1A646B for links and eyebrows
  • Sand only as a hairline, a seal ring, a glow or a badge sparkle
  • Red only for "Medical emergency? Call 9999" and the emergency callout

Do not

  • Pure black text, or grey text lighter than #4A5F72
  • Gold or sand text, gold gradients or "luxury" foil effects
  • Colours outside this palette (WhatsApp green only on the WhatsApp button)
  • A red cross or red plus anywhere
  • Dark full-width hero panels; the dark arch is the only deep surface in the hero
Logo

The arch logo in use

Redrawn as clean SVG from the old AI PNG, with the same arch, eight-point star, rod and serpent, ECG line, leaf and plus. Horizontal in the header (54px tall desktop, 44px mobile), stacked on the cover and About page, white on navy only, and the mark alone for the app icon.

For the coding agent: use the six SVG files in dr-james/logo/ (horizontal, stacked and mark, each in colour and white). Inline them so the wordmark uses Figtree from next/font; the white cut-outs follow --logo-ground, so set it to the surface colour behind the logo. Keep clear space equal to the medallion height on every side. Never stretch, recolour, add shadows or place the colour logo on navy. The 16px favicon needs a simplified mark (arch, star and rod only) before launch. Outline the wordmark text when exporting files for print.

09 / Quick answers

Questions patients ask

Native accordions (FAQPage JSON-LD), four on the home page with "See all FAQs". All answer text is in the HTML.

Where does Dr. James see patients?

At Badr Al Samaa Royal Hospital, Al Ghubrah Street, Muscat. Book by WhatsApp or phone on +968 9751 0975, or use the form on this site.

Do I need to fast before my visit?

Not for the consultation. Some blood tests, such as fasting sugar or cholesterol, need 8 to 10 hours without food. We tell you when you book if your tests need fasting. Water is fine.

What should I bring to my first visit?

Your old prescriptions, recent reports, the medicines you take (or photos of the packs), and your sugar diary or meter if you have diabetes.

Can Dr. James look after several conditions at once?

Yes. An internal medicine physician looks at diabetes, blood pressure, cholesterol, kidneys, liver and lungs together, so your medicines and tests work as one plan.

Callouts

Medical page notices

When to get help straight away. Call 9999 or go to the nearest emergency department if you have chest pain or pressure, sudden breathlessness, fainting, weakness on one side of the body, slurred speech, confusion, a seizure, or very high or very low sugar with drowsiness.

Medically reviewed by Dr. James Kumar Pallivathukkal, MD (Internal Medicine) · Oman MOH licence [CONFIRM] · Last reviewed [CONFIRM: sign-off date]

Tip. You do not need to fast for an HbA1c test. It shows your average sugar over the last two to three months.
